message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most popular sushi spots in Tokyo—ranging from Michelin‑starred temples to bustling conveyor‑belt joints. Whether you’re after a high‑end tasting menu or a casual bite, there’s something for every sushi lover.

| # | Restaurant | Type | Highlights | Location |
|---|------------|------|------------|----------|
| 1 | **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Classic & Michelin‑starred | Legendary 12‑course omakase; world‑famous chef Jiro Ono | Ginza (Tokyo 3‑Star Michelin) |
| 2 | **Sushi Saito** | Ultra‑exclusive | Intimate 10‑seat setting; meticulous nigiri | Minato |
| 3 | **Sushi Yoshitake** | High‑end | 3‑Star Michelin; seasonal, minimalist plating | Ginza |
| 4 | **Sushi Dai** | Conveyor‑belt & counter | Freshest tuna; long lines but worth it | Tsukiji Outer Market |
| 5 | **Sushi Zanmai** | Casual chain | 24/7 service; wide variety; affordable | Multiple locations |
| 6 | **Sushi Kyubey** | Classic | Elegant, high‑quality fish; long‑standing reputation | Ginza |
| 7 | **Sushi Natsume** | Intimate | 3‑Star Michelin; small, cozy setting | Shinjuku |
| 8 | **Sushi Masuda** | Traditional | 3‑Star Michelin; simple yet refined | Shibuya |
| 9 | **Sushi Tetsu** | Contemporary | 2‑Star Michelin; creative twists on classics | Shibuya |
|10 | **Sushi Kanda** | High‑end | 3‑Star Michelin; meticulous attention to detail | Minato |
|11 | **Sushi Iwa** | Modern | 2‑Star Michelin; innovative plating | Shibuya |
|12 | **Sushi Shun** | Classic | 2‑Star Michelin; renowned for its tuna | Ginza |
|13 | **Sushi Saito** | Ultra‑exclusive | 3‑Star Michelin; 10‑seat, no reservations | Minato |
|14 | **Sushi Saito** | Ultra‑exclusive | 3‑Star Michelin; 10‑seat, no reservations | Minato |
|15 | **Sushi Saito** | Ultra‑exclusive | 3‑Star Michelin; 10‑seat, no reservations | Minato |

### Quick Tips

- **Reservations**: For Michelin‑starred places, book months in advance (or use a concierge).  
- **Timing**: Many top spots open at 11 am; early arrival can secure a seat.  
- **Dress Code**: Some high‑end restaurants have a smart‑casual dress code.  
- **Payment**: Cash is still king in many sushi bars; credit cards may not be accepted.  

Enjoy your sushi adventure in Tokyo!
